pairs.together: Both lines set the impulse. You launch processes quickly and rarely wait for outside permission: there is usually more energy for starting than for following through.
pairs.strength: A fast start, readiness to take the initiative and to light others up for action.
pairs.friction: Overheating: much begun, little closed. The pace grows faster than the ability to hold it.
pairs.early: You speed up your speech and steps and take on new things without finishing the previous ones.
pairs.practice: Pick one started task and bring it to the end before launching a new one. Before every new start take a pause of one exhale.
pairs.question: What of what I started remains unfinished, and what of it is really needed?

pairs.together: The core launches, the vector shapes. The impulse gets support: ideas do not dissolve if you give them a form in advance: a deadline, a place, the size of a step.
pairs.strength: The ability to bring an impulse to a result when there is a plan and deadlines.
pairs.friction: The core hurries, the vector demands order. Hence irritation at the "slow", or, on the contrary, the clamp of "not ready yet".
pairs.early: Impatience appears toward a "too detailed" plan, or the start is postponed because of incomplete preparation.
pairs.practice: Before starting write three points: what you do, by when, and what the first fifteen-minute step is. Without this note, put the start off.
pairs.question: What form does my impulse need in order to live to see a result?

pairs.together: The core gives energy, the vector gives clarity of direction. A thought is quickly tested by action, and an action quickly gets its wording.
pairs.strength: Fast learning by practice and the ability to find words for action and allies.
pairs.friction: Many options and high speed: decisions are made on the fly and revised. The result is scattered focus instead of depth.
pairs.early: More tasks and tabs are open than you can keep in your head.
pairs.practice: Limit the number of active directions to three. Write a new idea down first, and act on it after the current step is finished.
pairs.question: Which three directions are the main ones for me now?

pairs.together: The core acts, the vector feels. The combination can join determination with attention to your state as long as they do not get in each other's way.
pairs.strength: You feel when to act and when to wait, and you act exactly as the situation requires.
pairs.friction: Sharp switches: a burst, then a drop. Will presses on the state, and the state brakes the will.
pairs.early: Irritation or apathy for no visible reason after a period of high activity.
pairs.practice: Plan your load in waves: a short burst, then a deliberate pause of the same length. Notice the signal of fatigue before it becomes a stop.
pairs.question: Which signal of fatigue do I miss most often?

pairs.together: The core gives support, the vector gives the launch. You hold the form reliably, and the vector nudges you to change it when it has grown old.
pairs.strength: Stability together with readiness to renew: you change without destroying the base.
pairs.friction: Habit argues with impulse: "it is fine as it is" against "time to move". The decision is postponed until the pressure grows.
pairs.early: You keep saying "later" although you understand that you are putting things off.
pairs.practice: Once a week choose one habitual order and consciously change one detail in it. Judge the result without haste.
pairs.question: What am I keeping out of habit, not out of meaning?

pairs.together: Both lines are about stability, order and density. You build and maintain well; reliability is your main resource.
pairs.strength: Reliability, patience, the ability to do work consistently and well.
pairs.friction: Stagnation: preserving becomes more important than developing. Changes are felt as a threat to the structure.
pairs.early: Refusing the new before the details have been considered.
pairs.practice: Add one small new action to your week that is not in your usual structure, and assess it after seven days.
pairs.question: What in my structure has not been reviewed for a long time?

pairs.together: The core gives form, the vector gives the structure of thought. Ideas quickly become plans: you know how to turn understanding into order.
pairs.strength: Clear structure and consistency: understanding turns into a working system.
pairs.friction: More plans than actions: the quality of preparation replaces the start.
pairs.early: You edit the plan instead of starting.
pairs.practice: Limit preparation by time (for example, twenty minutes) and take the first step even if the plan is incomplete.
pairs.question: Which first step am I putting off under the guise of preparation?

pairs.together: The core gives support, the vector gives recovery and flexibility. A firm base allows you to feel and to rebuild safely.
pairs.strength: Calm endurance and the ability to recover without losing the base.
pairs.friction: Heaviness: when the load exceeds the support, the system slides into viscosity, slowness and postponing.
pairs.early: Tasks are put off "until a better state".
pairs.practice: Choose one anchor habit, a simple ritual, and keep it regardless of mood. Plan the rest flexibly.
pairs.question: Which one habit holds me when everything else is unstable?

pairs.together: The core gives clarity and connections, the vector gives the launch. You see what to do and know how to begin: wording and action quickly find each other.
pairs.strength: You quickly formulate a goal and involve others.
pairs.friction: Words run ahead of deeds: discussion and explanation take energy that later is missing for execution.
pairs.early: The thought of the task comes more often than the task itself.
pairs.practice: After every important conversation or decision formulate one action you will take today and take it before the next discussion.
pairs.question: What do I talk about more than I do?

pairs.together: The core gives the structure of thought, the vector gives form and order. Clear ideas get a carrier: a document, a schedule, a rule.
pairs.strength: Logic and order: the complex becomes understandable and applicable.
pairs.friction: Rigidity: the structure is built before live information appears, and the plan is hard to change for new data.
pairs.early: Irritation when reality does not match the plan.
pairs.practice: Set a review point: in a week check the structure against the facts and change one part of it.
pairs.question: Which of my rules is due to be checked against the facts?

pairs.together: Both lines are about clarity, connections and structure. You quickly see patterns and know how to explain.
pairs.strength: Speed of understanding, breadth of connections, the ability to explain.
pairs.friction: The head is ahead of the body: much analysis, little support. The thought circles while the state does not change.
pairs.early: Many thoughts, little movement: the body stays in one position for long.
pairs.practice: Every day turn one conclusion into a bodily action: movement, water, a minute of silence. A thought is fixed by action.
pairs.question: Which of my latest conclusions has not turned into action?

pairs.together: The core gives clarity, the vector gives feeling and recovery. The combination can understand yourself and others and find words for a state.
pairs.strength: The ability to understand a state and find exact words for it.
pairs.friction: Analysis of feelings instead of living them: explaining a state becomes more important than changing anything in it.
pairs.early: You reread and rewrite the description of your state.
pairs.practice: When you notice tension, first do one bodily action for fifteen seconds and only then formulate what is happening.
pairs.question: What do I feel now, without naming the reasons yet?

pairs.together: The core gives sensitivity and recovery, the vector gives the launch. You sense the moment precisely and know how to begin when it has ripened.
pairs.strength: Precise choice of the moment: you feel when it is time and act decisively.
pairs.friction: Hesitation before the start: sensitivity to your state slows the decision, and then the impulse breaks through in a jerk.
pairs.early: The start is postponed until it "gets easier".
pairs.practice: Choose a fixed time to start an important task and begin regardless of mood, but with a minimal step.
pairs.question: What minimal step can I take today regardless of my state?

pairs.together: The core gives flow and recovery, the vector gives form. Sensitivity gets a frame: states do not spread but fit into an order.
pairs.strength: Emotional stability when there is order.
pairs.friction: The frame can press: order becomes a way of avoiding the state instead of helping it.
pairs.early: The routine starts to "press" even though you built it yourself.
pairs.practice: Leave one unstructured stretch of time in your schedule and do not fill it with tasks.
pairs.question: Where does order help me, and where does it hide my state?

pairs.together: The core gives perception and recovery, the vector gives clarity and structure. You feel and know how to describe what is happening.
pairs.strength: Depth of perception together with the ability to express it.
pairs.friction: Too many words around the state: it is hard to stop the analysis.
pairs.early: Every sensation wants to be explained with one more sentence.
pairs.practice: Keep the journal in short phrases: one state, one action, no more than two lines.
pairs.question: Which state can I simply note now, without explaining it?

pairs.together: Both lines are about perception, sensitivity and recovery. You read the environment well and know how to recover.
pairs.strength: Sensitivity, the ability to read the environment and to recover.
pairs.friction: Blurred boundaries: other people's states and circumstances take up a lot of room, and it is hard to hold your course.
pairs.early: Your mood starts to depend on other people's mood.
pairs.practice: Once a day mark one boundary: what you accept and what you leave outside. Say it to yourself in one phrase.
pairs.question: What of what is happening around me is not mine?
